points.quote: Each assignment or module may have different rules about whether AI tools can be used. If they can, it may also place restriction on how they can be used. Always check your assignment brief or ask your Module Convenor if you're unsure.
points.gist: Each assignment or module may have different AI rules and restrictions; always check your assignment brief or ask your Module Convenor if unsure.

points.quote: Not include materials generated by AI in your submissions.
points.anchor: What ‘Your Own Work’ Means When Using AI
points.gist: Unless otherwise noted, do not include materials generated by AI in your submissions.

points.quote: Not submit materials that you have written but that have been substantially altered by AI.
points.anchor: What ‘Your Own Work’ Means When Using AI
points.gist: Unless otherwise noted, do not submit your own writing that has been substantially altered by AI.

points.quote: By "substantially altered", we mean that your work should not be altered more than it would be by the spellchecking or grammar checking software that you would find in Microsoft Office products (i.e. a spellchecker that is not AI enabled).
points.anchor: What ‘Your Own Work’ Means When Using AI
points.gist: Substantially altered means altered more than a non-AI spellchecker or grammar checker in Microsoft Office would alter it.

points.quote: Some schools may also ask you to include a short declaration in your assessment submissions to confirm whether you have used generative AI and to what extent.
points.gist: Some schools may ask for a short declaration in submissions confirming whether and to what extent generative AI was used.

points.quote: Where required, the wording and expectations for these declarations will be specified in the assignment brief.
points.gist: Where a declaration is required, its wording and expectations will be specified in the assignment brief.

points.quote: Presenting a Generative AI output or another person’s work as your own is a breach of academic integrity.
points.gist: Presenting a Generative AI output or another person's work as your own is a breach of academic integrity.

points.quote: Engaging in discussion with AI tools as a "study buddy" (always double checking everything it outputs).
points.gist: Using AI tools as a study buddy in discussion is encouraged, always double checking everything it outputs.

points.quote: Searching for potential reading materials (again, always checking their relevance and refining your searches as you go).
points.gist: Searching for potential reading materials with AI is encouraged, always checking relevance and refining searches.

points.quote: Whether or not AI can be used, the final submission must demonstrate your own understanding, critical thinking, and academic judgement.
points.gist: Whether or not AI can be used, the final submission must demonstrate your own understanding, critical thinking and academic judgement.

points.quote: You can also visit our extensive prompt bank to see examples of appropriate use of AI which foreground and enhance your critical thinking skills.
points.gist: Students can visit the Kent AI Prompt Bank for examples of appropriate AI use that enhance critical thinking.

points.quote: The University is updating its regulations on academic misconduct to clarify Policy around the use of Generative AI in your learning and assessment.
points.gist: The University is updating its academic misconduct regulations to clarify policy on generative AI in learning and assessment.
